why: The findings represent three fundamentally distinct failure mechanisms: omitting required output completion/boundary markers, omitting explicit evidence categorization sections/headers (retrieved vs missing evidence lists), and failing to include required multi-hop logical mapping steps within the reasoning field.

parts.name: MISSING_TERMINAL_COMPLETION_MARKER
parts.definition: The model fails to output a required system boundary or terminal signal (such as `[[ ## completed ## ]]` or an explicit end marker) at the termination of its response.
parts.when_to_use: Use when the output content is generated but the prompt-mandated system completion or boundary tag at the end of the payload is missing.
parts.when_not_to_use: Do not use when text sections or structural list headings within the response body are missing.

parts.name: OMITTED_EVIDENCE_CATEGORIZATION_SECTION
parts.definition: The model fails to output mandatory explicit evidence lists or section headers (e.g., 'Retrieved required evidence documents' or 'Missing required evidence documents') in its reasoning or summary fields.
parts.when_to_use: Use when required evidence tracking headers/lists categorizing retrieved or missing documents are absent from the output.
parts.when_not_to_use: Do not use when missing a system boundary marker at the very end of response, or when failing to explain multi-hop reasoning logic.

parts.name: OMITTED_MULTI_HOP_REASONING_MAP
parts.definition: The model fails to map out the required multi-step/multi-hop verification chain in its reasoning field.
parts.when_to_use: Use when the reasoning field lacks the required step-by-step mapping of entity hops needed to verify a claim.
parts.when_not_to_use: Do not use when the reasoning includes the hop steps but omits explicit labeled headers for evidence document lists.
